A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
FDG PET/CT has excellent diagnostic sensitivity and specificity for lung metastasis in prostate cancer but that it is not a perfect test.
the presence of a Glut1-negative subcarinal lymph metastasis could not be excluded on PET–CT in a patient with a Glut1-positive lung metastasis from prostate cancer.
FDG PET/CT is a sensitive and specific tool for the detection of metastases from prostate carcinoma, but it may be less sensitive for small lymph node metastases.
The main takeaway from our work is that

FDG PET/CT is not always reliable in the evaluation of lung nodules and lymph node metastases in prostate cancer, and that Glut1 staining can be used as an adjunctive method to evaluate the likelihood of PET/CT visualization.
the Glut1 status should be assessed in all patients with prostate cancer and positive PET findings in the lung, even when there is no other evidence of distant metastases.
FDG-PET is highly sensitive for detecting lung metastases from prostate adenocarcinomas, but not all metastases will be FDG avid.
